title: When does the mean flow behave two-dimensionally?
purpose: Map finite-time transverse-disturbance growth and the accuracy of a matched autonomous 2D mean model, without using 3D energy alone as a closure criterion.
physical_choice: Deep-water monochromatic Stokes drift. UE0=-alpha us_ref and UL0=(waves-alpha)us_ref, so q0=-alpha us_ref_prime is retained, including for wave-off controls. Explicit viscosity and a documented compensating body force maintain the prescribed laminar background; eddies are freely evolving.
experiments: Seven background/current-amplitude cells with a matched 2D base, two tiny disturbances, and a finite disturbance.
Seed, viscosity, transverse-span, resolution, timestep and wave-off comparisons.
Native mean feedback, continuum scalar-vorticity budget, signed horizontal-scale transfer and packet-reference diagnostics.
limits: Finite-time 600 s experiments, not asymptotic stability boundaries or forced statistically steady turbulence.
Reference Re_lambda=U_2D_initial*lambda/nu; finite perturbations add energy, so achieved total Re differs and is reported.
Two tiny inputs have identical shapes and 100-fold energy separation; linearity must be checked before quoting a growth rate.
The width test changes allowed transverse modes as a physical parameter; it is not a pure numerical-convergence test.
Two selected cells have a second seed. The remaining parameter cells are single realizations.
The bounded-depth, variable-Stokes-shear flow does not inherit a universal Rossby threshold from rigid rotation.
The Ellingsen packet is a separate transient comparison with measured background vorticity and diagnostic residuals.
